sights.w: The thatched hut of the 17th-century haiku poet Mukai Kyorai, a disciple of Bashō, set among Sagano's fields. Small entry fee.
A Meiji-period street of preserved machiya at the far end of Sagano, below the torii of Atago Shrine. Many of the houses are now tea houses and shops. Free.

sights.address: Saga-Kamenoo-chō, Ukyō-ku, Kyoto (top of the Arashiyama bamboo grove path)
sights.w: A hilltop park at the top of the bamboo grove path, with a lookout over the Hozu gorge and fewer crowds. Free.
An ancient shrine to the gods of sake brewing and of childbirth, with a celebrated plum garden and a pond garden of irises and azaleas.

A sentō opened in 1923 in the former inn Funaoka-rō, registered as a Tangible Cultural Property, the third bathhouse in Japan to be listed. It has a karahafu entrance, carved coffered ceilings, majolica-tiled corridors and Japan's first electric bath.
